Looking at the net, label the vertical fold lines (which become the lateral edges) by their positions: left edge (x=0), first fold (x=1), second fold (x=2), right edge (x=3). When folded, x=0 and x=3 join, so the three lateral edges of the prism are at cross‑section corners C₀ (x=0/3), C₁ (x=1), and C₂ (x=2).

- **Top triangle:** attached to the top of the first rectangle (edge from C₀ to C₁ at the top). When folded up to form the top base, its apex P must land on the remaining top corner, C₂ (top of the fold line x=2).
- **Bottom triangle:** attached to the bottom of the third rectangle (edge from C₂ to C₀ at the bottom). When folded down, its apex Q lands on the bottom corner C₁.

Now track the labeled points:
- P becomes the top corner C₂.
- R is at the bottom of the fold line x=2, i.e., the bottom corner C₂.
- S is at the bottom of the edge x=3, i.e., bottom corner C₀.
- Q becomes bottom corner C₁.

The lateral edge through P (top corner C₂) runs down the fold line x=2 to the bottom corner C₂, which is exactly point R.

\boxed{B}
